question: A 36-year-old woman comes to the physician to discuss contraceptive options. She is currently sexually active with one male partner, and they have not been using any contraception. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. She is allergic to latex and copper. A urine pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following contraceptive methods is contraindicated in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Latex allergy -> Contraindication to latex diaphragm -> Unclear if spermicide is latex-free -> Uncertain -> 70% CHAIN: Copper allergy -> Contraindication to copper intrauterine device (IUD) -> Uncertain if other IUD types are suitable -> Uncertain -> 60% CHAIN: Smoking history -> Increased risk of cardiovascular events -> Contraindication to combined oral contraceptive pill -> 90% CHAIN: Negative urine pregnancy test -> No current pregnancy -> No contraindication to progestin-only pill -> 100% CHAIN: No known drug allergies -> No contraindication to condoms -> 70%
analysis: Considering the patient's history of latex allergy and copper allergy, the contraceptive method contraindicated in this patient would be the intrauterine device (IUD) as it can contain copper and may also have components made of latex.
